name: Tournament Desert
notes: Almost no terrain to hide behind — whoever wins the open-field engagement wins the map.
Expansion supply is exposed; raiding workers pays better here than anywhere.

name: Tournament Plains
notes: Long sight lines favour artillery and air; short-ranged armies must force the distance closed.
There is no chokepoint to turtle behind — mobile defence beats static defence.

name: Alpine Assault
notes: One real land route: static defence and artillery are disproportionately strong.
Thin supply rewards early expansion and punishes greedy tech.

name: Bitter Winter
notes: The crossings are the whole game — hold one and the map halves.
Garrisonable buildings near the middle make early infantry unusually valuable.

name: Winding River
notes: Bridges are hard chokepoints: mine them, defend them, or bypass them by air or tunnel.
Artillery across the river hits with impunity if you do not contest the bank.

name: Barren Badlands
notes: Several approach lanes mean a single defensive line does not cover you.
Scattered supply favours whoever can protect two piles at once.

name: Mountain Path
notes: Heavily choked: siege units and base defences dominate over manoeuvre.
With supply this thin, an early expansion denial usually decides it.

name: Tournament Island
notes: Water breaks up ground pushes — air and long-range units cross freely, armour does not.
Oil derricks are worth capturing early and worth raiding all game.

name: Silent Woods
notes: Tree cover and winding lanes make ambushes and stealth armies much stronger here.
Scout constantly — an army can sit fifteen seconds from your base unseen.

name: Flash Fire
notes: Open flats: the fight is decided by army composition, not by position.
Central supply is a permanent contest — plan to fight for it, not to own it.

name: Killing Fields
notes: Rich supply lets both sides tech fast — expect superweapons and late-game armies.
Garrisonable farms along the lanes reward keeping infantry in the army all game.

name: Forgotten Forest
notes: Narrow trails and heavy cover: this is the best stealth map in the stock rotation.
Detection is not optional here, whatever you are playing against.

name: Dark Mountain
notes: Sparse supply and hard chokes reward a fast expansion followed by a turtle.
High ground positions give artillery a commanding field of fire.

name: Leipzig Lowlands
notes: Urban garrisons make infantry and garrison-clearing units decisive.
Streets funnel armour — bring something that clears buildings or you will stall.

name: Scorched Earth
notes: Long travel times mean reinforcements arrive late — forward production matters.
With six players, the diplomatic and positional read matters as much as the build.

name: Homeland Alliance
notes: Eight players and rich supply means the game goes long — build for the late game.
Expect superweapons; spread your base from the first dozer.
